 Order

This is the first application filed by the applicant under Section 482 of B.N.S.S. for grant of anticipatory bail apprehending his arrest in connection with Crime No.0450/2025 at Police Station Kolar Road Bhopal Sehari, District Bhopal (M.P.) for the offence punishable under Sections 420,
467, 468, 120-B, 406 of IPC.

sentences.text: 2. As per the prosecution story, it is alleged that applicant deceived and cheated the complainant.

Therefore, the offence has been registered against the present applicant under the aforesaid section.
3.
Learned counsel for the applicant submits that applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case.

It is submitted that applicant has given money to the complainant Lakhan Kawde for purchase of edible oil but complainant did not supply the edible oil therefore NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:18053 2 MCRC-59777-2025 complainant has given cheque to the applicant but the same was dishonoured.
Thereafter, applicant has filed a complaint under Section 138 of Negotiable Instrument Act and as a counter blast complainant has lodged this false case.
Offence under section 406 and 420 cannot be made.
Custodial interrogation of the applicant is not necessary.
The applicant is ready to cooperate in the investigation.

In support of his submission, learned counsel for applicant has placed reliance on the decision of Hon'ble Apex Court in Arshad Neyaz Khan Vs. State of Jharkhand and Another reported in 2025 SCC OnLine SC 2058.

sentences.text: Therefore, it has been prayed that the applicant may be granted anticipatory bail.

4. On the other hand, learned counsel for State as well objector have opposed the grant of bail to the applicant and submitted that applicant has not submitted any documentary evidence to show that he has given money to the complainant.

It is submitted that when complainant has given notice to Shahid Khan vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/78632597/
1 the complainant then complainant has given detailed reply in which all facts relating to fraud played with the applicant are mentioned.

entities.text: Shahid Khan vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The said reply has not been submitted by the applicant which shows that applicant has not come to the Court with clean hands.
Complainant had also filed application under Section 156(3) of Cr.P.C. before the concerning JMFC.

It is further submitted that applicant along with other co-accused persons fraudulently obtained money from the complainant by forging contract dated 25.05.2023 and, therefore, case has been registered against the applicant and other co- accused persons under Sections 420, 467, 468, 120-B, 406 of IPC.
Applicant is absconding
and custodial interrogation of the applicant is required in this NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:18053 3 MCRC-59777-2025 case.
Hence, the applicant does not deserve grant of anticipatory bail.

5. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.
6.
Looking to the overall facts and circumstances of the case as well as allegation levelled against the applicant, this Court is not inclined to grant anticipatory bail to the applicant.
7. Accordingly, this MCRC stands dismissed.
